family_rule: A family is the tuple of axis values in family.out.json 'axes', one value for every axis below. Two submissions are in the same family if and only if their axes maps are equal. The family name, parent, seeds and every parameter (u, k, mu, table contents, QROAM block size k, angle bits, segment counts, threshold choices, qubit layout) are not part of the family: changing them is calibration within a family, never a new family. A value is added to an axis only when the architecture differs in how the walk step is built, with a citation or a written definition that says what differs.
versioning: MAJOR changes when a value is removed or a signature's meaning changes; MINOR when a value, axis or rule is added or a reserved value becomes active; PATCH for wording. A family declares taxonomy_version; the harness accepts it when the MAJOR number equals this file's.

strengths.exact: One predicate is both necessary and sufficient: it holds if and only if the value applies. Holds -> Verified, fails -> Contradicted.
strengths.necessary: Every correct circuit with this value satisfies the predicate. Fails -> Contradicted. Holds -> DeclaredOnly (it does not identify the value).
strengths.sufficient: When the predicate holds the value applies. Holds -> Verified. Fails -> DeclaredOnly.
strengths.necessary+sufficient: Separate necessary and sufficient predicates. Necessary fails -> Contradicted; sufficient holds -> Verified; otherwise DeclaredOnly.
strengths.declared: No predicate over CircuitFacts separates this value from its siblings. Always DeclaredOnly unless a compatibility rule or reserved status contradicts it.

predicate_language: {"all": [p...]}, {"any": [p...]}, {"not": p}, {"cmp": {"field": path, "op": op, "value": v}} or {"cmp": {"sum": [path...], "op": op, "value": number}}. op is one of == != > >= < <=. A path is dot-separated through the serialized CircuitFacts (src/facts.rs); key matching ignores case, '_' and '-' so 'op_counts.HMR' matches kind 'Hmr'. A missing key in a map of counts reads 0; any other missing or null field is unknown. Unknown never contradicts and never verifies. Predicates over segment_* fields read the submitter's own Segment labels (op kind 40), which are hints: they can contradict a claim the labels themselves refute, but they prove nothing about unlabelled or mislabelled ops.

axes.definition: How SELECT applies the chosen term's system operator.

values.definition: Unary iteration over term indices; each indicator controls that term's Pauli string on the system register.

values.definition: Each term is a product of up to four Majoranas whose indices are loaded as data; SELECT applies each selected Majorana by one unary pass over the 2n Majorana indices (Z string plus X/Y).

values.definition: SELECT is Toffoli-free: the term's Pauli masks (or their span coordinates) were loaded as data before SELECT, with the control folded into the data, and CX/CZ/S gates from data qubits apply the term.

citations.supports: Pure-Clifford SELECT: the QPE control is folded into the lookup so the masks are zero when it is off (LiH). Unpublished.

signature.proves: Necessary: the ops labelled SELECT are Toffoli-free and act on the system. signature.cannot_show: Segment hints are the submitter's labels: segments_validated checks their structure (one prepare, select, unprepare; system ops only in select), not that each Toffoli sits where it logically belongs.

values.definition: DF or THC SELECT: rotate the system into the basis of each number-type factor (a DF leaf eigenvector or a THC factor vector) with a network of Givens rotations whose angles are loaded as data, apply the Z operator, rotate back.

citations.supports: Block-encoded, basis-transformed Majorana operator via a sequence of Majorana (Givens-type) rotations with data-looked-up angles.
QROM outputs rotation angles; controlled rotations rotate the basis at cost N(i-2); Z applied; rotations reversed.
THC select: a QROM outputs the rotations for mu (then nu), rotate with cost N(i-2), apply Z, invert the rotations.

signature.proves: A DF or THC circuit that passed validation and used Givens ops applied its rotated operators through the harness's Givens primitive, the only basis-rotation mechanism in the op set. (1.1.0 widened the encoding clause from df to df or thc; no df or sparse verdict changes.)
signature.cannot_show: The network's shape (how many rotations, which order).

values.definition: Nested DF: each leaf's one-body operator is block-encoded with Givens networks, the inner register is reflected, and the same block encoding is applied again, block-encoding the Chebyshev polynomial 2 O_l^2 - 1 (spec/DESIGN.md section 16).

The 1/8 becomes 1/4 by 'the oblivious amplitude amplification, Chebyshev polynomial technique'; the reflection on the second register only, between two applications of the rotations.

rules.reason: A sparse spec's lanes are parsed only by the flat alias or the sparse symmetry alias.
DF terms are rotated operators; df-pair-alias-v1 (flat) and df-nested-alias-v1 (nested) map lanes to them.
A flat pair lane map admits no Reflect (the harness rejects it), so SELECT cannot be nested.
A nested lane map requires the nested structure, so SELECT is the nested composition.
Sparse terms are Majorana monomials, applied without basis rotations.
DF terms are number operators in a rotated basis.
Sparse terms need no arbitrary-angle rotation.
DF basis changes are Givens rotations; the Givens op is the only rotation primitive.
Alias sampling reads keep and alt from a table (Babbush et al. 2018 Sec. III.D, step 2).
Alias sampling reads keep and alt from a table.
Alias sampling reads keep and alt from a table, and the rotation angles are data.
Both alias levels read keep and alt from tables, and the rotation angles are data.
THC terms are ordered products of rotated operators; only thc-pair-alias-v1 maps lanes to them in this release.
THC terms are number operators in the factors' rotated bases.
THC basis changes rotate onto non-orthogonal factor vectors with the Givens op.
Alias sampling reads keep and alt from a table, and the rotation angles are data.
An sos-sa spec's lanes are parsed only by sa-nested-alias-v1.
The spectrum-amplified lane map requires the nested structure around one Reflect.
The sum-of-squares generators are applied in rotated bases, twice around a reflection.
The generators' basis changes are Givens rotations.
Both alias levels read keep and alt from tables, and the rotation angles are data.
The power-product lookup ends by measuring its ancillas in the X basis (Gidney 2025 App. A.4).
